concept.name: Composite profile
concept.definition: A Market Profile or volume profile built by merging multiple sessions into one distribution, so that the combined structure of a multi-day balance, bracket, or swing becomes visible. Its composite point of control and value area aggregate activity across all included sessions and are treated as higher-weight references than single-session levels.
concept.intuition: One day's profile shows one battle; the composite shows the whole campaign — where the market has collectively done its business over weeks.
concept.mechanics: TPO letters or volume from each included session are pooled into a single price distribution (platforms provide split/merge tools for this); the resulting composite POC, value area, and nodes are read as the governing structure of the larger auction.
concept.failure_modes: The choice of which sessions to merge is discretionary and changes every derived level; composites over long spans mix different volatility regimes and market participants, diluting the meaning of 'value'.
concept.misconceptions: A composite is not automatically more 'true' because it covers more data — including irrelevant history creates levels with no living participants behind them.
concept.example: Three weeks of overlapping ES sessions are merged into one composite whose POC sits at 4,470; when a breakout attempt stalls, traders watch whether price accepts back below that composite POC.
